question_details.resolution_criteria:
This question is a subquestion of a group question. This subquestion specifically targets the option 'Rabi Lamichhane'. The resolution criteria for the parent question is below. 

This question resolves as **Yes** for the individual who, after September 11, 2025 and before January 1, 2026 takes the [oath](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Nepal_2016#s852) of office and secrecy as the new [Prime Minister of Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Nepal) and wins a vote of confidence in the House of Representatives as required by [section 76](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Nepal_2016#s795) of the Constitution of Nepal. The question resolves as **No** for everyone else. If none of the listed candidates fulfills the criteria during that time period, then the question resolves as **No** for every option.
question_details.fine_print: This is a Group question, so you do not have to assess probabilities for every option. summary: All seven forecasting experts agreed that the probability of Rabi Lamichhane becoming the next non-caretaker prime minister of Nepal before January 1, 2026, is extremely low. The consensus is rooted in several key factors: (1) Lamichhane's recent incarceration for embezzlement/fraud, with ongoing legal clouds making it difficult or impossible for him to secure eligibility or parliamentary support; (2) the current status quo of a caretaker government led by Sushila Karki, whose specific mandate is to oversee elections scheduled for March 2026, with both domestic elites and international actors favoring stability and consensus candidates; (3) the parliamentary math is unfavorable for Lamichhane, as his party has suffered significant resignations and lacks the numbers to form a majority coalition; (4) Nepal's historical base rates indicate that contentious outsider or populist figures with legal troubles rarely, if ever, ascend to the premiership in short-order post-crisis caretaker periods. Some experts noted that while Lamichhane has some Gen Z and anti-corruption protester support, this is insufficient against entrenched institutional, legal, and elite resistance. All experts described 'yes' scenarios as requiring a highly unlikely series of events, including total collapse of the caretaker government, Lamichhane's legal exoneration and release, mass mobilization in his favor, and rapid realignment among MPs to support his candidacy, none of which have credible indications of occurring. Assigned probabilities varied slightly but clustered between 1% and 2%, reflecting near-unanimity on the vanishingly small chance of Lamichhane assuming office before the resolution date.
